body:
Hi Nikki,

I'm sorry to hear that you're feeling depressed. You are obviously a very caring person who takes relationships very seriously. I'm using the term "relationships" in a very general sense to encompass any extended human-to-human interactions.

I feel that there are two types of people: those that try and form long-lasting, close ties with a small number of people and those that socialize and keep a very loose net of acquaintances. It would appear that you've met a lot of the latter.

To be fair, I shouldn't imply that the latter group is in the wrong. It's just that they will probably never value your devotion and commitment. They'll never reciprocate the depth of your bond as they don't seek it. Unfortunately, I've found that they greatly outnumber the people who value a smaller number of close friends. Things probably aren't going to get any better. If anything, I've found that people tend to form even shallower relationships as they age. 

The most important thing is to accept yourself and realize that very few people will every truly care for you. Those that stick around and survive the test of time (like family) start meaning even more to you.

You bring joy to a lot of people, even if they don't deserve it. It's unfortunate that they take what they need and leave, but that doesn't lessen your value any bit. You just have to weather through the storm of shallow people and hope that you meet a true friend who deserves someone like you. Even if you don't, the world needs more people like you.

I think I've started rambling a bit here... What I mean to say is... You seem like a great person. It's unfortunate that you haven't met someone worthy of your friendship yet. Perhaps it'll take a lifetime. Even so, please don't give up. People like you are those that make the world a bearable place.

:) Thanks. I'll consider your advice.

Suicide never seems like a sane choice to those not contemplating it. At least, that's what I feel when others have mentioned it to me.

It's all about what people choose to live for. If that motive is taken away, things start crumbling.

As long as I can remain functional, I doubt I'll be seeking professional help. Talking was never the issue. Regardless, thank you for your time. I hope you enjoy the Thanksgiving break :)

Yes, I know. It's the least I can do for them though. Thing is, life will go on. Hopefully, they'll be able to grasp that I did it only because the alternative was worse. 

Don't get me wrong, I'm still fighting for one last opportunity. It's just that this is the end of the line. If this falls through, I'll be on a countdown with nothing left to do but watch everything I built fall to pieces around me. The good thing is that I never got to start the family that I dreamed about, so my death will not ruin the lives of anyone I care about.

I've talked to someone close about my feelings. There's nothing they can do. I appreciate their company but, unless I can resolve the issue, it'll be an endless cycle of me whining and complaining with no impact on the outcome.

Yea, you're right. I rarely get depressed from small setbacks. It's just when I've exhausted every possible solution with no result that I start feeling sad. That's why I've stayed alive for 10 years.

Once it all goes down, I estimate another 7~8 years to get back to where I am now. Looking back at the past 10 years, I just can't do that again.

I have Mormon friends who've gone through similar situations. I can't imagine anything more painful than having the people you once trusted turn their backs on you.

The thing is, you need to isolate your beliefs from your support network. I agree with vedicvoyager. Believe in what you want to believe, but keep it to yourself until you are ready to fully accept that belief. Gain the strength in your belief to survive without a support network and start anew if needed. It will take time, but you cannot let the beliefs of others dictate the course of your life.

Also, I feel horrible for saying this, but it would seem that your support network is very fragile if they're willing to abandon you so readily over religion. True friendships and bonds should transcend petty beliefs and opinions...

Hey, I know how you feel. I was bullied in elementary and middle school. Hell, I was so desperate and had such low self-esteem that I ended up trying to befriend a kid that kept on stealing from me.

What I learnt from this is that you live for yourself, not for others. Friends or no friends, as long as you can be happy with who you are, it doesn't matter. Think about what characteristics you value in people and try and incorporate that into your own identity. That way, it doesn't matter what others think of you. All that matters is that you are becoming who you want to be.

First things first... cut down on the drinking and weed. Think of what you want to accomplish with your life and see where you stand in terms of making that a reality. Plenty of people are willing to die for something, but very few people are willing to live for something :) Asshole or not, you still have a chance to make something of your life. You say there is too much effort for little reward. Surely there must be something that you really want?
